extracted.intended_audience: physician-scientists (postdoctoral and early-career) applying for the Burroughs Wellcome Fund Career Awards for Medical Scientists (CAMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting a CAMS grant application to support physician-scientists transitioning from advanced postdoctoral/fellowship training to early faculty service. Covers eligibility, application materials, formatting, budget limits, reporting, and award logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The Career Awards for Medical Scientists (CAMS) provides $700,000 awards over five years for physician-scientists committed to an academic career to bridge advanced postdoctoral/fellowship training and the early years of faculty service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is highly competitive and intended specifically to support transition from training to independent faculty research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of research eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is only for individuals in basic biomedical, disease-oriented, or translational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health services research and policy are explicitly ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree-type eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be physician-scientists; Ph.D.-only applicants are not eligible. Pharm.D. or Pharm.D., Ph.D. degree holders are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your background is in physical/mathematical/computational sciences or engineering addressing biological questions, consider Career Awards at the Scientific Interface instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-author publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have at least one first-author publication to be competitive and eligible to apply for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared first authorship counts. Accepted/in-press manuscripts count; bioRxiv preprints count. Unaccepted/unpublished manuscripts do not count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research effort expectation (75% protected time)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the expectation that 75 percent of the applicant's time will be devoted to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants do not need to already have 75% protected time at submission if that time can be negotiated upon award; letters of support or an offer letter should demonstrate this. For surgeons and all specialties, 75% is the expectation regardless of specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional approval and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be approved by an official at the institution responsible for sponsored programs; an Institutional Certification Form completed and signed by an authorized signing official is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Institutional Certification certifies (a) the university’s non-profit status as a degree-granting institution and (b) the applicant meets eligibility and residency requirements. An application is not considered complete without it. Emailed/mailed/faxed institutional certification forms will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature Page requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Signature Page Form provides a signature line for the Applicant and must be uploaded with the applicant’s signature by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is not considered complete without the Signature Page form. Emailed/mailed/faxed signature pages will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-nomination and nomination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates do not need to be nominated by their institution; since August 2015 eligible candidates may self-nominate by submitting a full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if self-nominating, institutional approval (see Institutional Certification) is still required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of training environment/institution restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The training environment (mentor and institution) is an integral part of the proposal and cannot be changed after submitting the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you move to a new institution after submission, you will not be eligible to interview even if invited. Invitations to finalists are based on information submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-investigator policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAMS grant program does not allow co-investigators on the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the proposal as a single-investigator application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor letter(s) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one mentor letter of recommendation may be submitted. That letter should be from the person designated as your primary postdoctoral mentor or faculty sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a co-mentor/secondary mentor, both may co-write and sign one mentor letter (acceptable), or the co-mentor may instead write one of your three additional recommendation letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support/Recommendation letter submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All support letters must be uploaded and attached to your application and submitted electronically by the application deadline. Emailed, mailed, or faxed letters will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should be addressed to the CAMS Advisory Committee and must be uploaded by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research plan page limit and counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The research plan has a six-page maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures, tables, graphs, diagrams, and pictures included in the research plan count toward the six-page limit. A bibliography and glossaries of technical abbreviations/terms do not count toward the page limit and are acceptable if they clarify the proposal to the general reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on additional appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not include materials beyond those requested by the application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including additional materials may disqualify you from the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative budget required
rubrics_metrics.description: A tentative budget associated with your project plan must be included with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a budget summary consistent with the project and the program's listed limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and fringe benefit limits (postdoc phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the awardee elects to utilize the postdoctoral portion of the award (up to two years): a maximum of $90,000 may be used for salary and fringe benefits combined during year one of the postdoctoral phase; a maximum of $95,000 may be used for salary and fringe benefits combined during year two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are strict limits for the postdoctoral portion of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and fringe benefit limits (faculty phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the faculty portion of this award, a maximum of $59,500 may be used annually towards the named investigator's salary and fringe benefits combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning for the faculty phase must respect this annual limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caregiver expense allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Caregiver expenses may be budgeted up to $5,000 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is separate from the salary and fringe limits and can be utilized during any portion of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font, spacing, and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard 11- or 12-point type for text and no smaller than 9- to 10-point type for figures, legends, and tables. The text must be single-spaced, with one inch or larger margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The font size requirement is strictly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and deadline firmness
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted electronically via Proposal Central by the application deadline; paper applications will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application deadline is firm. You may start and save an application and return later, but once submitted it cannot be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No changes after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your application is submitted, it cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan carefully; verify all proposal details, mentor/institution information, and uploaded letters before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single application per candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not submit more than one application for the CAMS program in a given cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submitted application is the only one from you for that deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report requirements (annual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit an annual progress report that includes a written report on the progress of the original or approved update to research project aims, an updated biographical sketch, a letter of support, and any recent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress reports are due annually on November 1st and must be submitted through Proposal Central. Advisory Committee and staff rely on these reports to evaluate progress; late reports may result in withheld payments or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting requirements (biannual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are required to update award spending in the Proposal Central budget summary twice each year and provide up-to-date spending information from the previous six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial reports are due biannually on February 1st and August 1st and must be submitted through Proposal Central. Failure to submit will result in interruption or cancellation of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award portability and institution transfer conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is portable and most awardees will change institutions to begin a faculty appointment, but transferring is not guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new institution must demonstrate commitment via offering a tenure-track or equivalent appointment and significant start-up money, and BWF must approve the transfer. Transfers during the faculty portion of the award are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension (family commitments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may interrupt the award for family commitments and BWF will allow a no-cost extension of up to two years during the award term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact program staff to arrange extensions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent funding and award conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients may obtain funds from other sources for research in the same or similar areas so long as there is no conflict with meeting the terms of BWF’s award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award recipients may not hold concurrent BWF awards or NIH K99/R00, NIH DP5, or similar Early Independence awards; certain K awards (K08, K12, K21, K23) are compatible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF does not currently have a cap on reapplying; as long as a candidate remains eligible, they can reapply an unlimited number of times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility must be met for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility questions and contacting BWF
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for reading published guidelines and FAQs to determine eligibility before contacting BWF staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have unique training paths or experiences not fully addressed, contact cams@bwfund.org for guidance. BWF will prioritize questions not already clearly addressed; do not request exceptions to clearly stated guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of non‑tenure-track startup packages
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess eligibility for applicants with non-tenure track offers, BWF reviews startup packages on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit your full offer letter (you may redact salary or confidential portions) to the CAMS team no later than 2 weeks prior to the application deadline. Letters will be kept confidential and used only for eligibility review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing letters of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation should be addressed to the CAMS Advisory Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must be uploaded and attached to the application by the deadline; mailed or emailed letters are not accepted.
